mainTopic: The order of inheritance: why a son outranks a brother, why the daughter comes before the father, and why the father comes before the deceased's brothers
overview: This amud continues the question of who inherits first. The גמרא first asks whether a son ranks above a brother just by counting advantages, two for the son against one for the brother. It answers that the son's advantage with שדה אחוזה really comes from the rule that a son cancels יבום. Next it suggests reading 'שארו' so that the father comes before the daughter, and rejects this: for יבום a son and a daughter count the same, so for נחלה they count the same too. Then it suggests that 'שארו' only puts the father ahead of his own brothers. It rejects this as well, since the father's brothers inherit only through the father, so no פסוק is needed for that. When the order of the פסוקים seems to put the father last, the גמרא answers that they are not written in order. Finally it brings a ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, who learns from the word 'והעברתם' that only a daughter takes the inheritance away from the father. The amud ends with a challenge to that reading, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The son has two advantages, the brother only one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is the son ranked above the brother just because the son has two advantages and the brother only one?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because here (with the son) there are two advantages, and here (with the brother) there is only one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the son really ranks above the brother just because he has two advantages and the brother has only one. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the son was shown to step into his father's place in two ways (יעוד and שדה אחוזה). The brother steps into his brother's place in only one way (יבום). The גמרא asks whether simply counting 'two against one' is what decides it. Step 2 shows the real reason is different.

keyTerms.meaning: here (this case)
two (advantages)
one (advantage)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of an argument. The 'two' are the son's advantages (יעוד and שדה אחוזה). The 'one' is the brother's advantage (יבום).

phrases.english: for here there are two,
phrases.notes: The son stands in for his father in two ways, יעוד and the ancestral field; the brother has only one, יבום.

phrases.english: and here only one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the counting argument begun before this section: son versus brother.
steps.raayaObject: That a son ranks above a brother
steps.raayaSupportSource: Counting advantages: the son has two (יעוד and שדה אחוזה), the brother has one (יבום)

steps.title: The ancestral field comes from the same idea as יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the son's advantage with שדה אחוזה is not a separate point. It comes from the rule that יבום only happens when there is no son.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ancestral field itself comes from this same reason. The תנא holds: is there any יבום except where there is no son? So where there is a son, there is no יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ancestral field is not really an extra advantage. It grows out of the יבום rule itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא takes it as given that a son cancels יבום. That shows a son is closer to the father than a brother is. This is why only a son, and not a brother, counts as the father for redeeming the field. So the ancestral-field rule depends on the יבום idea and is not a second, independent proof.

keyTerms.meaning: an ancestral field (inherited land that was dedicated to the Temple)
levirate marriage: a brother marries the widow of his brother who died without children
he holds it as established
is there anything at all... (a rhetorical question)

steps.whatToRemember: A son cancels יבום, so a son is closer to his father than a brother is. Even the ancestral-field rule is built on this.

phrases.english: The ancestral field itself,
is from this same reason;
for the תנא holds it as established:
is there any levirate marriage at all
except where there is no son?
So where there is a son, there is no levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה גּוּפַהּ, מֵהַאי טַעְמָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains that one of the son's 'two' advantages actually comes from the יבום rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows one point depends on another, so it is not an independent advantage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ancestral field counts as a separate, second advantage of the son.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ancestral-field rule comes from the fact that a son cancels יבום. So the son's closeness rests on this one idea.

steps.title: Suggestion: the father should come before the daughter too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading 'שארו' as the father in a way that would put the father ahead of the daughter, while 'הקרוב' still keeps the son first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'his kinsman' (שארו) is the father, which teaches that the father comes before the daughter. Could he even come before the son? The verse says 'the closest' (הקרוב): whoever is closest comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another possible reading of the פסוק. On this reading the father would inherit before the daughter of the man who died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father has so far been placed only ahead of the brothers. This suggestion uses the same words to push the father ahead of the daughter as well. The word 'הקרוב' would still stop him from passing the son, because the son is closer.

keyTerms.meaning: say instead (suggesting another reading)
his kinsman (במדבר 27:11)
the closest relative
one might have thought
therefore the verse says

phrases.english: Say: 'his kinsman': this is the father,
teaching that the father comes before the daughter.
One might think he comes before the son?
So the verse says: 'the closest':
whoever is closer comes first!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: ״שְׁאֵרוֹ״ – זֶה הָאָב, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָאָב קוֹדֵם לַבַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a different reading of the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that puts the father ahead of the brothers only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words could also put the father ahead of the daughter, with 'הקרוב' still keeping the son first.

steps.title: For יבום son and daughter are equal, so for inheritance too
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. A daughter cancels יבום just like a son does, so for נחלה a daughter counts like a son, and the father does not come before her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since for יבום a son and a daughter are the same, for inheritance too a son and a daughter are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that the father comes before the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום does not happen if the man who died left either a son or a daughter. So the Torah treats them the same as 'continuing' the man who died. This sameness carries over to נחלה: the father cannot come before the daughter any more than before the son.

keyTerms.meaning: since
they are like each other (equal)
inheritance
regarding the matter of

steps.whatToRemember: A daughter, like a son, comes before the father in inheritance, because for יבום both count the same.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the הלכה that the deceased's children, sons or daughters, inherit before his father.

phrases.english: Since regarding levirate marriage
a son and a daughter are equal,
phrases.notes: Either one, son or daughter, means there is no יבום.

phrases.english: regarding inheritance as well,
a son and a daughter are equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּלְעִנְיַן יִבּוּם – בֵּן וּבַת כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the suggestion in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that the father comes before the daughter
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores that son and daughter are equal for יבום, and that sameness carries over to inheritance.

steps.title: Maybe 'his kinsman' only puts the father ahead of his own brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading 'שארו' as teaching only that the father comes before the father's brothers. Under this reading, 'הקרוב' would keep the deceased's brothers ahead of the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: 'שארו' means the father, and it teaches only that the father comes before the father's brothers. You might think the father also comes before the deceased's brothers. So the פסוק says 'הקרוב': whoever is closer comes first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to read the פסוק. In this reading the father inherits after the deceased's brothers instead of before them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now 'שארו' was taken to put the father ahead of the deceased's brothers. This suggestion shrinks it: the father only beats his own brothers. The word 'הקרוב' is then used to keep the deceased's brothers, the closer ones in this reading, in front of the father.

keyTerms.meaning: His kinsman, a word in the פסוק that is read here as the father
The father's brothers, the deceased's uncles
Brothers, here meaning the deceased's own brothers
The nearest one; the closer relative inherits first

phrases.english: But say: "His kinsman" — this is the father,
teaching that the father comes before the father's brothers.
One might think he should also come before the brothers?
phrases.notes: "The brothers" here means the deceased's own brothers.

phrases.english: So the verse says: "the nearest" —
whoever is closer comes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the father's place compared to the daughter, the גמרא now questions his place compared to the brothers.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the father inherits before the brothers of the deceased
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'שארו' could teach only that the father beats his own brothers, so it is no proof that he beats the deceased's brothers.

steps.title: No פסוק is needed for the father to beat his own brothers
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. The father's brothers inherit only through the father, so they obviously cannot inherit while he is there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father's brothers do not need a פסוק. Through whom do the father's brothers come to inherit? Through the father. If the father is standing right here, could his brothers inherit?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the new reading. The father beats his own brothers by plain logic, so 'שארו' must be teaching something more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The uncles are related to the deceased only through the father. Their right to inherit comes from him, so they cannot go ahead of him. A פסוק is not wasted on something this obvious, so 'שארו' must put the father ahead of the deceased's brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not need a פסוק; this is obvious by logic
By the power of, through whom someone gets his right
He is standing, meaning he is present and alive

phrases.english: The father's brothers do not need a verse;

phrases.aramaic: אַחֵי הָאָב מִכֹּחַ מַאן קָא אָתוּ –
phrases.english: the father's brothers, by whose power do they come to inherit?
By the power of the father;

phrases.aramaic: קָאֵי אָב, קָא יָרְתִי אַחֵי הָאָב?!
phrases.english: the father is standing here, and the father's brothers inherit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reading suggested in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that 'שארו' only puts the father ahead of his own brothers
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule is obvious by logic, since the uncles inherit through the father, so a פסוק would not be needed to teach it.

steps.title: But the פסוקים put the father after the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: in the פסוקים, 'שארו' (the father) comes only after the brothers and the father's brothers, which suggests he inherits after them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוקים are not written that way, since it says: 'And if his father has no brothers,' and only after that comes 'שארו'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with putting the father ahead of the brothers: the order of the פסוקים seems to put him last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists the deceased's brothers, then the father's brothers, and only then 'שארו'. If the list follows the order of inheritance, the father should come after all of them. This attacks the conclusion of step 6 from the order of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוקים, the verses
They are not written that way

phrases.english: But the verses are not written that way —
as it is written: "And if his father has no brothers, etc."!
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:11. The father, as 'שארו', shows up only after the father's brothers in the list.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 6 that the father comes before the brothers.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 6's logic that the father's brothers cannot inherit while the father is alive, which is the basis for putting the father ahead of the deceased's brothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's order of the inheritance list puts 'שארו' last, after both sets of brothers.

steps.title: The פסוקים are not written in order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the פסוקים in this section are not written in the order of inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוקים are written out of order.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the order in the Torah here is not the order of who inherits first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since logic forces the father ahead of his own brothers, the list cannot be in strict order. So the father's place at the end does not show he inherits last, and he can come before the deceased's brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in their proper order

steps.whatToRemember: The father inherits before the brothers of the deceased. The פסוקים that seem to put him last are not written in order.

phrases.english: The verses are written not in their order.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the order of the text
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the פסוקים is the order of inheritance, so the father comes last.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוקים are not in order, so the father comes before the brothers.

steps.title: Another source: the word 'והעברתם'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי learns from 'and you shall pass' that only a daughter takes the inheritance away from the father, not brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא learns it from here, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי taught this: 'If a man dies and has no son, (then you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter)'. Where there is a daughter, you pass the inheritance away from the father. But where there are brothers, you do not pass the inheritance away from the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, from a ברייתא, for the rule that the father comes before the deceased's brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'והעברתם', you shall pass, only about the daughter. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי reads this as taking the inheritance away from the father, who would otherwise come first. Since this word appears only with the daughter, brothers do not take the inheritance away from the father.

keyTerms.meaning: A teacher of the time of the משנה; here, the author of the ברייתא
Passes over, takes away from one person and gives to another
Inheritance

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a direct source in the פסוק for the father's place ahead of the brothers, so the rule does not rest only on logic and saying the פסוקים are out of order.

phrases.english: And this tanna brings it from here —

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei taught this:

phrases.aramaic: ״אִישׁ כִּי יָמוּת וּבֵן אֵין לוֹ וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: "If a man dies and has no son, etc." —
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:8. The rest of this פסוק says 'you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter'. Everywhere else in the section the Torah says 'give', and only here does it say 'pass'.

phrases.aramaic: בִּמְקוֹם בַּת אַתָּה מַעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב,
phrases.english: where there is a daughter, you pass the inheritance away from the father,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מַעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִן הָאָב בִּמְקוֹם אַחִין.
phrases.english: but you do not pass the inheritance away from the father where there are brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source for the same rule proven in steps 6-8.
steps.raayaObject: The father inherits before the brothers of the deceased
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'והעברתם' in במדבר 27:8, used only for the daughter

steps.title: Maybe the daughter only takes the inheritance from the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't read 'והעברתם' as teaching only that a daughter comes before the brothers, instead of before the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not say: when there is a daughter, you pass the inheritance away from the brothers to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא from Step 9 and suggests a different meaning for the word 'והעברתם'. This sets up an answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said the word teaches that only a daughter takes the inheritance away from the father, and brothers do not. The גמרא asks: maybe the word is about the brothers instead, meaning a daughter comes before the deceased's brothers. If so, the word proves nothing about where the father stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But why not say... (introduces a different way to read the source)
In a case where there is a daughter
Pass the inheritance (move it away from one person to another)
Brothers (here, the brothers of the person who died)

phrases.english: But why not say: in a case where there is a daughter,
phrases.notes: This picks up the word 'והעברתם' (and you shall pass) from the ברייתא in Step 9.

phrases.english: you pass the inheritance away from the brothers to her,
phrases.notes: In other words, the word would only teach that a daughter comes before the brothers. It would teach nothing about the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: בִּמְקוֹם בַּת אַתָּה מַעֲבִיר נַחֲלָה מִן הָאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the ברייתא in Step 9 reads 'והעברתם'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי's reading in Step 9, that 'והעברתם' teaches the daughter takes the inheritance away from the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'pass' could just as easily mean the daughter takes the inheritance away from the brothers. Then it gives no proof that the father comes before the brothers.
